extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR reviewers, small_biotech management, potential development partners and investors evaluating a commercialization plan for an antiviral drug candidate
extracted.subtask_description: A commercialization plan for a small biotechnology company (FCCDC) describing the regulatory pathway, clinical development timelines, manufacturing, IP, market/customers, funding models, and revenue strategies to advance an antiviral drug candidate (FC-10696) toward IND, NDA and commercialization, including use of the Animal Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-IND meeting with FDA and IND/FIH timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-IND meeting will be held with the FDA prior to initiation of IND enabling studies, to obtain guidance as to proper preclinical and clinical study design and requirements. We expect to file an Investigational New Drug (IND) in ~2Q/2024, with First in Human (FIH) dosing to begin ~1Q/2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pre-IND meeting to confirm designs of preclinical and clinical studies; follow the timeline to IND filing and FIH dosing unless partnership changes who leads development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory approval pathway: Animal Rule (21 CFR Part 314 Subpart 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since our primary indication is as a Marburg antiviral medication, effectiveness of our candidate may not easily be determined in human clinical trials for ethical reasons. Thus, we will resort to the 'Animal Rule' (21CFR Part 314 Subpart 1) as the regulatory pathway for approval of this drug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan efficacy demonstration using relevant animal models per the Animal Rule; expect NDA approval to be based on animal efficacy plus human safety data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I clinical evaluation design and endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Phase I clinical evaluation will take place in normal individuals looking for safety and tolerability in a single ascending and multiple ascending dose format and drug-drug interactions. Clinical read-outs will include standard hemodynamic parameters involved in cardiovascular safety testing. Adverse events would be monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated study duration ~12 months, enroll ~40 participants, estimated cost $3 million; design should capture safety, tolerability, PK and DDI data needed for regulatory filing and to inform later studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II clinical trial design and endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II trial beginning ~1Q/2027 will be an intervention trial for healthy patients with human T cell leukemia virus (a virus with a similar mode of egress to Marburg). A dose of candidate compound would be administered orally with a placebo. The endpoints would be change in viral load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated study duration ~10 months, enroll ~140 participants, estimated cost $10 million; select appropriate surrogate human model where direct human efficacy trials for Marburg/Ebola are not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: NDA filing content and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A New Drug Application (NDA) will be filed with the U.S. FDA containing all of the CMC and other ICH regulatory and safety pharmacology documentation required for commercialization. This would be scheduled to occur at ~2Q/2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare full CMC, safety pharmacology, toxicology and bridging documentation per ICH; coordinate timing with animal efficacy and human safety data to support NDA submission under the Animal Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial FDA approval target
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial FDA approval would be for use as an antiviral therapeutic agent for Marburg infection. This would occur on or about 1Q/2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan commercial launch preparations and post-approval requirements around this projected approval window; note dependence on successful animal-rule pathway and regulatory review timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profile — Efficacy (% survive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred: >95% survival. Minimally acceptable: >85% survival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set preferred and minimally acceptable efficacy thresholds to drive go/no-go decisions during development and to support regulatory and reimbursement arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profile — Efficacy (virus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred: Undetectable levels of virus. Minimally acceptable: Undetectable levels of virus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieve robust virologic endpoints (undetectable viral load) as part of efficacy profile; relevant especially when using surrogate clinical models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profile — Adverse events
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred: Comparable to placebo. Minimally acceptable: Minor adverse events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for safety profile similar to placebo; minimize adverse events to aid regulatory acceptance and adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profile — Administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred: Oral. Minimally acceptable: Oral. Note: An IV formulation may be preferable for the extremely ill, and a liquid formulation useful for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral administration is prioritized for ease of distribution and use; maintain flexibility to develop IV or liquid formulations for specific populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profile — Dosing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred: Once daily. Minimally acceptable: Twice a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simpler dosing (once daily) preferred to improve adherence and deployment in outbreak settings; accept twice daily as minimally acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profile — Drug resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred: None. Minimally acceptable: None.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design compound and combination strategies to minimize emergence of resistance; consider combination therapy approaches akin to HIV cocktails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profile — Stability / packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred: No special packaging required. Minimally acceptable: Modest precautions acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for formulations that avoid cold-chain and special packaging to facilitate distribution in remote/low-resource settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing capability and GMP strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our current laboratory capabilities enable us to prepare 100 g batches of any candidate, to a high level of purity (>99%). As we require GMP-grade drug substance, we will engage an appropriate contract research organization who is properly certified for this type of chemistry project. Once a facility is selected, we will perform a site visit to ensure that our projects are performed under standard good laboratory practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document current non-GMP capacity and plan to engage GMP-certified CROs; perform vendor qualification and site visits to ensure compliance with GLP/GMP and scalability needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market and potential customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary customers: BARDA; other potential governmental partners include NIAID, Office of Biodefense Research (OBRA), DOD, DTRA, USAMRIID, DSTL, CDC. Potential private partners include small biotech (Siga, Tekmira, Chimerix, MappBio Pharm, Athene, Biocryst, Tetraphase) and large companies (Merck, Johnson & Johnson, GSK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target government biodefense procurement and advanced development funding (BARDA) and cultivate partnerships with companies already focused on biothreat therapeutics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive differentiation / value proposition
rubrics_metrics.description: There are currently no other agents that inhibit virus egress being developed as broad spectrum RNA antiviral agents. An oral drug product based on FC-10696 is potentially first-in-class, broad-spectrum for RNA viruses with PPxY motifs, differentiates from vaccines by oral administration and economic manufacturing and ease of distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight first-in-class mechanism, oral route, broad-spectrum potential, and logistical advantages over biologics/vaccines to investors, partners and purchasers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property protection strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: FCCDC and the Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania obtained U.S. Patent 10,160,756 (Dec 25, 2018) covering earlier analogs. FC-10696 and its present suite of analogs are outside the scope and will be subject to new composition of matter applications. We will file PCT applications and pursue patent protection in major foreign markets, including Europe, Asia and BRIC countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue prosecution of provisional and composition-of-matter filings during the grant period; plan international filings (PCT and national phases) to protect key markets; leverage leadership patent experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization models (three options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model #1: Licensing for all indications to a mid-level or large pharmaceutical company (upfront cash + royalties + milestones). Model #2: FCCDC continues development through Animal Rule efficacy and Phase I safety studies to derisk the asset, then monetize (funding from corporate partners, VC, government, or foundations). Model #3: Hybrid — transition/licensing to a development partner prior to conclusion of Phase I or during Animal Rule studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timing and partners to maximize transaction value; pursue derisking as appropriate to attract better licensing terms or choose to advance further in-house depending on resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding strategy and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial funding has come from prior Phase I STTR/R41 grants. Future funding sources include licensing deals, BARDA contracts, DTRA, CDC, NIH, foundation support, corporate partners, angel/VC investment, and NIAID Phase IIB grants for small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue a mix of government advanced development funding (e.g., BARDA), grants, and private financing; tailor funding strategy to chosen commercialization model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue stream expectations and mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary revenue likely from licensure to the US government and Department of Defense, with licensing deals generating upfront fees, milestone payments and royalties. Additional revenue may come from sale of the U.S. Neglected Disease Priority Review Voucher if NDA approval is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model revenue scenarios under different commercialization models (out-licensing vs in-house development); quantify potential voucher value and timing as part of valuation discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory incentives to pursue
rubrics_metrics.description: Most important: agents for Ebola and Marburg are eligible for the U.S. Neglected Disease Voucher program. FCCDC will file for Orphan Drug designation for Marburg or Ebola infection. The FDA frequently waives application fees for small businesses (<500 employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively apply for incentives (priority review vouchers, orphan drug designation, fee waivers) to reduce costs and increase asset value; document eligibility and expected benefits (market exclusivity, tax credits, grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with key opinion leaders, academic investigators and external partners
rubrics_metrics.description: FCCDC will actively solicit support from academic investigators and clinicians who manage anti-infective clinical trials and will engage key opinion leaders as part of the Scientific Advisory Board to select clinical safety study design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use KOLs and clinician collaborators to design trials, facilitate site selection, and strengthen credibility with funders and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing specialized preclinical and CMC tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: There are a number of companies that perform highly specialized tasks important for regulatory approval, such as those addressing preclinical toxicity, safety pharmacology and genotoxicity, while other companies have substantial CMC expertise for drug substance and drug product manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and manage specialized CROs for tasks beyond internal capacity; leverage existing relationships and perform vendor qualification to ensure data quality for regulatory submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production scale-up and quality attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: We can prepare 100 g batches to >99% purity in-house. For GMP-grade production, work with certified CROs. Maintain high purity standards and ensure supply-chain readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan scale-up steps from laboratory batches to GMP manufacturing, including analytical methods, impurity profiling, and supplier qualification to support CMC sections of regulatory filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and awareness-building activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase awareness of the candidate and platform compounds in the scientific community by publications in appropriate peer-reviewed journals and presentations at national scientific meetings. Engage internal business development function and CFO in partner/investor discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use publications, conferences, and KOL advocacy to generate interest; build dedicated business development capabilities to manage partner negotiations and investor outreach.
